previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 3.7 ng/mL detected on routine screening. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable at that time. A transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was arranged, and the patient was advised to await results.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (earlier timepoint):
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The tumour demonstrates organoid arranged glandular tubules. A cribriform pattern is present. Perineural invasion is not identified.

Biopsy 2 (most recent timepoint):
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The tumour demonstrates tubules. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is present. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, mid right.

Summary:
The histological grade group remains ISUP 1 across both timepoints, although the growth pattern has shifted from organoid arranged glandular tubules with cribriform features to tubules with the new emergence of perineural invasion.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): Timepoint 1 — grade group 3; Timepoint 2 — grade group 3.
